en.headline: Grave of late actress Linda Lin Dai vandalised at Happy Valley cemetery
en.dek: Cemetery staff found graffiti and cement covering the marble altar of the four-time Asia Pacific Film Festival best actress; an 87-year-old man was arrested in connection with damage to a nearby grave.
body: The grave of late Hong Kong actress Linda Lin Dai at St Michael’s Catholic Cemetery in Happy Valley has been vandalised. Cemetery staff discovered graffiti and that the marble altar had been covered with cement, the first such incident at the site according to the cemetery office.

Lin Dai, who won the Asia Pacific Film Festival Best Actress award four times and died in 1964 at the age of 29, is buried at the cemetery. The office posted a notice seeking to contact her family about repairs and reported the matter to police on the day it was found.

A nearby religious order grave was also damaged. Police arrested an 87-year-old retired man on 4 August in connection with the second grave. He denied intentional damage and said he had been carrying out maintenance work. The Wan Chai district crime squad is investigating his motive.
The cemetery said security patrols and CCTV cover the grounds. The Lin Dai grave has been cordoned off pending restoration once family arrangements are confirmed.

zh.headline: 跑馬地林黛墳墓遭塗鴉及英泥覆蓋 87歲翁涉破壞鄰近墳墓被捕
zh.dek: 聖彌額爾天主教墳場發現四屆亞太影展影后林黛墓碑遭塗鴉，雲石拜台被英泥覆蓋；警方另就鄰近修會墳墓破壞拘捕一名退休男子。
body: 一代影后林黛長眠跑馬地天主教聖彌額爾墳場的墳墓遭人破壞。墳場辦事處發現墓碑有塗鴉，雲石拜台被人用英泥覆蓋，並指屬首次發生。
林黛原名程月如，四度奪得亞太影展影后，1964年逝世，享年29歲。辦事處已於發現當日報警，並張貼通告聯絡家屬安排維修。
附近一個修會墳墓亦遭破壞。警方於8月4日拘捕一名87歲退休男子，涉破壞該墳墓。男子否認刻意毀壞，稱當時只是進行維修工作。案件由灣仔警區刑事調查隊跟進，正調查動機。
墳場表示場內有保安巡邏及閉路電視覆蓋。林黛墳墓現已圍封，待家屬安排後進行修復。
